adaptations: Each original parameter expansion is a separately reported Rust #[test]. Tests invoke real crypto, recovery, storage, HTTP/CLI domains and inspect owned filesystem effects; no Python runtime or parity oracle is invoked.

Native test-support observers run at real encryption, atomic commit, rollback restoration, data/config fsync, descriptor publication and cleanup boundaries. Observers are scoped by thread and explicitly propagated through worker-thread boundaries; product builds exclude them.

Hard exits use owned native subprocesses re-executing the exact same reported test case. A worker exits 73 at the original corresponding checkpoint; the parent verifies the exit and independently recovers/asserts all planted credentials. No helper tests or extra reported cases are introduced.

Concurrency cases use actual native root transaction locks and separate threads coordinated after a real credential commit, checking that the competing read/write remains blocked until the migration publishes its descriptor.

Native CLI child_command places the unlock in the child environment without argv exposure. The browser receives an already decrypted Profile and an actual bound native credential-relay endpoint; launch options use that relay without plaintext credentials. The production restrict_environment helper is called by real Adapter::spawn_admitted and tested dynamically to remove master/API/updater credentials while preserving unrelated settings.
Original optional cryptography/FastAPI skip conditions have no corresponding native skip: Rust crypto and HTTP dependencies are always present in this target.
Frozen Linux errno IDs remain stable on Windows; unsupported fsync cases inject equivalent native FlushFileBuffers errors (InvalidInput/Unsupported) while asserting the same tolerance contract.

Arbitrary fixture passwords and salts use stable synthetic old/new pairs across recovery modules to share the native KDF cache; wrong-password values, role assertions, source parameter IDs, data shapes and fault stages are preserved.

Original RollbackFailed exception assertions map to RecoveryErrorKind::RollbackFailed with the public atomic::RollbackFailed carrier; tests inspect original syscall errno, failed path/errno, Error::source chain and successful restoration of all other files.
